papers.title_in_file: Enhancing Quantum Adversarial Robustness by Randomized Encodings
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sections I to V (introduction, Theorems 1, 2 and 4 statements and sketches, conclusions); appendix proofs not read
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proposing random unitary and quantum-error-correction encoders as a defense of quantum classifiers against adversarial perturbations.

assertions.value: The paper proves that random global and local unitary encoders lead to exponentially vanishing gradients (barren plateaus) for any variational quantum circuit that aims to add adversarial perturbations, independent of the input data and of the inner structure of the adversarial circuits and the quantum classifiers.
assertions.anchor: Abstract; Sec. III, Theorems 1 and 2, p.1 and p.4
quotes: we rigorously prove that both global and local random unitary encoders lead to exponentially vanishing gradients (i.e. barren plateaus) for any variational quantum circuits that aim to add adversarial perturbations
independent of the input data and the inner structures of adversarial circuits and quantum classifiers
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 1 and 2, Sec. III (the local-encoder case carries assumptions on the adversarial circuit)
assertions.reader_inference: The local-encoder result holds under assumptions on the adversary's circuit, so 'any' in the abstract is wider than Theorem 2.

assertions.value: The authors show that concatenating only O(log log(n)) levels of quantum error correction encoders is sufficient to bound the adversarial risk below a constant value, for local unitary adversarial perturbations and encoders unknown to the adversary.
assertions.anchor: Sec. I and Sec. IV, Theorems 3 and 4
quotes: it is sufficient to concatenate only O(log log(n)) levels of QEC encoders to bound the adversarial risk below a constant value
We show that random black-box quantum error correction encoders can protect quantum classifiers against local adversarial noises
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 3 and 4, Sec. IV

assertions.value: The authors state that their discussion focuses on quantum supervised learning, and that an experiment demonstrating the defense strategies against adversarial perturbations remains to be carried out.
quotes: our discussions in this paper mainly focus on quantum supervised learning scenarios
it is also of crucial importance to carry out an experiment to demonstrate our defense strategies against adversarial perturbations
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of scope and limits, Sec. V

papers.title_in_file: Machine Learning on Heterogeneous, Edge, and QUantum Hardware for Particle Physics (ML-HEQUPP)

papers.what_it_is: A community white paper on research priorities for ML on edge, heterogeneous and quantum hardware in particle physics experiments.

assertions.value: The paper states, citing other work, that all existing quantum processor technologies remain within the NISQ regime, where error correction is costly and computational advantage is limited to specialized tasks.
quotes: remain within the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) regime, where error correction is costly and computational advantage is limited to specialized tasks

assertions.value: The authors state that near-term quantum approaches are not necessarily expected to outperform classical pipelines broadly, and that a quantifiable and generalizable quantum advantage over state-of-the-art CPU/GPU methods for quantum annealing in these experimental problems remains to be seen.
quotes: While near-term quantum approaches are not necessarily expected to outperform
A quantifiable and generalizable quantum advantage over state-of-the-art classical CPU/GPU methods in such experimental challenges remains to be seen.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' assessment in a white paper, no experiment behind it

assertions.value: The paper describes itself as a community-driven white paper that identifies and prioritizes research and development opportunities in hardware-based ML systems and corresponding physics applications, and states that quantum computing remains in early stages for practical high-energy physics deployment.
quotes: This white paper presents a community-driven vision to identify and prioritize research and development opportunities in hardware-based ML systems and corresponding physics applications
While quantum computing remains in early stages for practical HEP deployment

papers.title_in_file: Kernel Density Matrices for Probabilistic Deep Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Section 1, Section 3 (experiments), Section 4 (conclusions); Section 2 derivations and proofs skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A quantum-inspired classical framework that extends density matrices to reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces for differentiable density estimation, inference and sampling.

assertions.value: The authors report that a classifier built on kernel density matrices performs on par with a deep model of comparable complexity on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10, and that maximum-likelihood fine-tuning for generation slightly degrades classification performance.
assertions.anchor: Sec. 3.1 and Table 1, p.11 to p.12
quotes: The results show that the performance of the KDM based model is on par with a deep model of comparable complexity.
Observe that the classification performance ML-KDM slightly degrades with respect to KDM
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results of one study; accuracy figures are in Table 1 and are not restated here

assertions.value: The authors report that on learning from label proportions, kernel density matrices reach a competitive performance equal to that of a state-of-the-art method designed for that task.
quotes: The results show that KDM has a competitive performance equal to that of a state-of-the-art method explicitly designed for the LLP task.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one study

assertions.value: The authors state that the model is a quantum-inspired machine-learning method, and that the experiments are exploratory and illustrate the potential of the framework.
assertions.anchor: Sec. 1.1 and Sec. 4, p.2 and p.14
quotes: The model presented in this work can be regarded as a quantum-inspired
The exploratory experiments shed light on the potential of this framework
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope, Sec. 1.1 and Sec. 4

papers.title_in_file: Opportunities and Challenges for Data Quality in the Era of Quantum Computing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sections I, II (to II-A), III (experimental study, results), IV, V; reference list and taxonomy figures not read in detail
papers.what_it_is: A vision and survey paper on quantum computing for data quality and anomaly detection, with a small quantum reservoir computing experiment on stock volatility regimes.

assertions.value: The authors report that in their volatility regime change experiment, quantum reservoir computing performs at least as well as classical reservoir computing and outperforms classical linear models in the task.
quotes: These results demonstrate that quantum reservoir computing performs at least as well as classical reservoir computing, outperforming classical linear models in the task
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one preliminary experiment on one dataset
assertions.reader_inference: The authors' own caveats (noiseless simulation, small qubit count) limit how far this extends.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum circuits were simulated with Qiskit without noise, that the work is preliminary, and that only 9 qubits were used. The data are 29 publicly traded stocks in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, over five years from 2015 to 2020.
assertions.anchor: Sec. III-B, III-C and results discussion
quotes: the model are simulated with Qiskit without noise.
especially considering that this is preliminary work and we used only 9 qubits
We focus on 29 publicly traded stocks in the Dow Jones Industrial Average stock market index, spanning five years from 2015 to 2020.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own description of their setup and limits, Sec. III

assertions.value: The authors state that their review found that purely quantum-native anomaly detection solutions have not yet been established, and that practical realizations of quantum replacements for ARIMA subroutines remain speculative.
quotes: indicating that purely quantum-native solutions have not yet been established
practical realizations remain speculative and require further investigation into quantum circuit design and error mitigation strategies
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' reading of the literature; no systematic protocol is reported in the quoted passages

assertions.value: The authors report that their first literature review identified 44 classical anomaly detection approaches that could benefit from replacing computing-intensive subroutines with quantum methods.
quotes: Identifying 44 classical anomaly detection approaches that could benefit from using the corresponding quantum methods to replace their computing-intensive subroutines.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own literature review count; the potential benefit is not demonstrated

papers.title_in_file: Verifying Fairness in Quantum Machine Learning
papers.what_it_is: A formal framework and tensor-network algorithm for verifying individual fairness of noisy quantum machine learning decision models.

assertions.value: The paper proves that checking fairness of a noisy quantum decision model reduces to a variant of distinguishing quantum measurements, and shows as a corollary that quantum noise can improve fairness.
assertions.anchor: Sec. 1 contributions; Theorem 1 and Theorem 2, Sec. 5
quotes: We prove that for a given (noisy) quantum decision model, checking the fairness can be reduced to a variant of distinguishing quantum measurements (states)
As a corollary, we show that quantum noise can improve fairness.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 1 and 2, Sec. 5

assertions.value: The authors report experiments on quantum (noisy) decision models with 8 or 9 qubits for income prediction and credit scoring on real-world data, and say the efficiency of the algorithm is shown by a class of random quantum decision models with 27 qubits.
quotes: The effectiveness of our algorithm is confirmed by experiments on quantum (noisy) decision models with 8 or 9 quantum bits (qubits) for income prediction and credit scoring on real-world data
its efficiency is shown by a class of random quantum decision models with 27 qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results of one study, run on simulation

assertions.value: The authors state that there are still no public benchmarks for quantum decision models, that the medium-scale models were generated with randomly sampled parameters, and that further investigation is required to understand the detected bias kernels through more experiments on real-world applications.
quotes: There is still no public benchmarks for quantum decision models.
The efficiency of our algorithm is then demonstrated on these models with randomly sampled parameters.
further investigations are required to better understand the bias kernels detected by our verification algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of setup and limits, Sec. 6 and Sec. 7

papers.title_in_file: QuProFS: An Evolutionary Training-free Approach to Efficient Quantum Feature Map Search
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Related Works, Preliminaries, Experiments and results, Conclusion and Limitations; supplementary proofs and appendix tables not read in detail
papers.what_it_is: A training-free evolutionary quantum architecture search method that ranks circuits with proxy metrics to find quantum feature maps for quantum kernel classification.

assertions.value: The authors report that QuProFS offers the fastest runtime among the quantum architecture search benchmarks while maintaining comparable accuracy, and that circuits run on IBMQ devices maintain competitive accuracy on par with simulator results.
assertions.anchor: Conclusion; Experiments, Performance on Real Quantum Hardware
quotes: Our results show that this method offers the fastest runtime among QAS benchmarks while maintaining comparable accuracy.
Despite the presence of noise and decoherence, QuProFS circuits maintain competitive accuracy, demonstrating robustness and practical viability on real quantum hardware
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results of one study on binary classification tasks; the figures are in tables not restated here

assertions.value: The authors state that classical kernels, particularly RBF-based ones, still outperform quantum counterparts on real-world data.
quotes: classical kernels (particularly RBF-based ones) still outperform quantum counterparts on real-world data
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical statement by the authors in their conclusion

assertions.value: The authors state that the reliability of training-free proxies remains uncertain because high proxy scores often fail to predict downstream accuracy, and that all two-qubit gates are restricted to adjacent qubits to respect native connectivity.
quotes: The reliability of training-free proxies remains uncertain, as high proxy scores often fail to predict downstream accuracy, especially across datasets or hardware.
we restrict all two-qubit gates to operate on adjacent qubits, respecting native connectivity constraints
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of limits, Limitations and Future Work

assertions.value: The authors state that they evaluate the approach on classification tasks using a quantum support vector machine across artificial and quantum-generated datasets.
quotes: We evaluate our approach on classification tasks (using quantum support vector machine) across diverse datasets using both artificial and quantum-generated datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own evaluation setup, Abstract

papers.title_in_file: Guided sampling ansatzes for variational quantum computing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Section I, results on the hydronium cation (Figs. 3 to 6 text), hardware description; derivations not read in detail
papers.what_it_is: A variational quantum computing method using guided sampling ansatzes, demonstrated on a small molecule with trapped-ion hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the hydronium cation, with only 200 circuit executions per structure on the IonQ Aria quantum computer, their calculations produced total energies around the relaxed structure with errors well below the chemical accuracy threshold.
quotes: found that with only 200 circuit executions per structure on the IonQ Aria quantum computer, our calculations produced total energies around the relaxed structure with errors well below
Figure 5 also shows that our calculations of the total many-electron energy exceed chemical accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small molecule on one device
assertions.reader_inference: The energy optimization is done classically on samples taken from the QPU, per the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that the primary purpose of the QPU calculations is to identify the most important Fock states through the obtained measurement samples, and that the error increases with increasing bond length.
quotes: the primary purpose of the QPU calculations is to identify the most important Fock states through the obtained measurement samples
The error increases with increasing bond length as the number of Fock states needed to approximate the ground state to within a given tolerance also increases.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' description of how the method and the result are scoped, Sec. III and Fig. 5 caption

assertions.value: The authors state that it remains unclear how the accuracy depends on the system and sample sizes, which they leave for future work.
quotes: Although our results are promising, it remains unclear how the accuracy depends on the system and sample sizes.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit, Sec. III

papers.title_in_file: QuanBench: Benchmarking Quantum Code Generation with Large Language Models
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sections I, II, IV (setup), V (overall performance, task coverage), VI (threats to validity), VIII (conclusion); detailed error-analysis tables read in part
papers.what_it_is: A benchmark of quantum programming tasks in Qiskit for evaluating the code generation of large language models.

assertions.value: The authors report that the evaluated LLMs have limited capability to generate correct quantum code: Pass@1 accuracy remains below 40%, the highest Pass@5 score reaches only 50%, and even the best model reaches only an average Process Fidelity of 51.8%.
quotes: The Pass@1 accuracy remains below 40%, and the highest Pass@5 score reaches only 50%.
even the best model reaches only an average Process Fidelity of 51.8%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one benchmark study on one task set

assertions.value: The authors state that QuanBench includes 44 programming tasks built on the Qiskit framework (version 0.46.0), covering quantum algorithms, state preparation, gate decomposition and quantum machine learning, and that nine LLMs were evaluated.
quotes: QuanBench includes 44 programming tasks that cover quantum algorithms, state preparation, gate decomposition, and quantum machine learning.
Built on the Qiskit framework (version 0.46.0)
We evaluate nine recent LLMs
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Abstract and Sec. I

assertions.value: The authors state that the benchmark is limited to the Qiskit framework and that the number of quantum machine learning tasks remains limited because of the scarcity of publicly available implementations.
quotes: First, the benchmark is currently limited to the Qiskit framework.
the number of quantum machine learning tasks remains limited due to the scarcity of publicly available implementations
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limits, Sec. VI
